Traditional German Stollen

Served at: First Sunday of Advent

Makes 1 large Stollen (about 12-15 slices)Prep 45 min (plus 3-4 hours rising time)Cook 50-60 min

Stollen is a rich, fruit-studded yeast bread, traditionally enjoyed throughout the Advent season in Germany and beyond. Its distinctive shape, often dusted heavily with powdered sugar, is said to represent the Christ Child wrapped in swaddling clothes. Serving Stollen on the First Sunday of Advent marks the official start of the festive Christmas preparations and is a cherished tradition.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) dark rum or brandy
  • 1/2 cup (80 g) golden raisins
  • 1/2 cup (80 g) dark raisins
  • 1/4 cup (40 g) dried currants
  • 1/4 cup (40 g) candied orange peel, diced
  • 1/4 cup (40 g) candied lemon peel, diced
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) slivered almonds
  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, lukewarm (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (1 standard packet)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, divided
  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon ground cardamom
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1 large egg, at room temperature
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened, plus 1/2 cup (113 g) melted for brushing
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) powdered sugar, for dusting

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the rum or brandy with golden raisins, dark raisins, currants, candied orange peel, and candied lemon peel. Stir well, cover, and let soak for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight.
  2. In a separate small bowl, combine the lukewarm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon of the granulated sugar. Stir gently and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  3. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, remaining granulated sugar, salt, cardamom, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
  4. Pour the yeast mixture into the flour mixture. Add the egg, vanilla extract, and the 1/2 cup (113 g) softened butter. Mix with a wooden spoon or a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
  5. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, or until smooth and elastic. If using a stand mixer, knead on medium-low speed for 6-8 minutes.
  6. Drain the soaked fruits, discarding any remaining liquid. Add the drained fruits and slivered almonds to the dough. Knead for another 2-3 minutes until the fruits and nuts are evenly distributed.
  7. Lightly grease a large bowl. Place the dough in the bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  8. Punch down the dough gently. On a lightly floured surface, roll or pat the dough into an oval shape, about 12x8 inches (30x20 cm).
  9. Along the length of the oval, create a shallow indentation just off-center. Fold the smaller side of the dough over the larger side, creating the traditional Stollen hump. Gently press the edges to seal.
  10. Carefully transfer the shaped Stollen to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let rise again in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until visibly puffy.
  11. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
  12. Bake the Stollen for 50-60 minutes, or until golden brown and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. If it browns too quickly, tent loosely with aluminum foil.
  13. Immediately after removing from the oven, brush the hot Stollen generously with the 1/2 cup (113 g) melted butter, ensuring all surfaces are coated.
  14. While still warm, sift a thick layer of powdered sugar over the entire Stollen. Let cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving. For best flavor, wrap tightly and let sit for 1-2 days before serving.

Tips

  • For an extra festive touch, you can roll out a 4-ounce (113 g) log of marzipan and place it in the center of the dough before folding, creating a marzipan core.
  • Stollen improves with age; wrap it tightly in foil and then in plastic wrap, and store in a cool, dry place for up to 2-3 weeks. The flavors meld beautifully.
  • Ensure your yeast is fresh and your milk is at the correct temperature for optimal dough rise.
